messages:
andrea: Heads up — noticed enforcement 429s while the metering pipeline is showing ~6-8m ingestion lag for org=acme-corp. Saw customer report and reproduced in staging.

sam: Can you paste the enforcer log snippet and which node?

andrea: Enforcer log (snippet):
```
[enforcer-12] 2026-03-17T22:14:03Z WARN quota_reject org=acme-corp key=client-xyz tokens=120 reason=quota_exceeded
[enforcer-12] check_read: last_flush_ts=2026-03-17T22:07:22Z cached_tokens=0
```
We got 429s at T=22:14 but the pipeline shows those requests landing at T=22:18 in clickhouse.

mira: Consumer metrics from kafka-metering show: consumer_lag=410k msgs (~7m) at current throughput. Our clickhouse flush batching is 30s, but the end-to-end from topic->agg->write can spike to several minutes on backpressure. Also retention for late events is 5m.

devops-bot: Alert: meter-ingest-lag high for topic "meter-events" (avg lag 6.8m) — PagerDuty P12345 triggered.

harry: We've seen similar. Fast mitigation is to increase the enforcer's "pending TTL" to 10m so enforcement tolerates delayed canonical writes. Downside: could allow short double-spend/double-accept in burst scenarios.

yuki: Wait — how would TTL cause double-spend? Our enforcer reads redis aggregates; if pipeline is late, enforcer will tend to undercount and allow, not reject. The symptom here is rejects while later the pipeline records usage — sounds like a race where enforcement applies a strict subtraction based on a different window.

andrea: Sketch timeline:
T0: requests arrive (some accepted, some rejected)
T1: enforcer checks local counters (stale), rejects some requests -> 429 returned
T2: pipeline processes queued events and writes canonical usage -> dashboard now shows usage for those requests that were previously rejected. So customer saw 429s but we later have records of their calls. The mismatch is enforcement rejecting before pipeline has visibility of prior allowances or the prior reservations.

sam: Could this be the reservation/ack race? We use an async reserve->ack path: proxy increments local reserved counter and writes to topic. If the write fails or is delayed, the enforcer might take a conservative path and reject subsequent requests. Also at-least-once semantics in the ingest path could complicate dedupe.

mira: Two root causes IMO: 1) consumer lag + batch flush delay; 2) enforcement and metering use slightly different aggregation windows (enforcer uses 1s rolling, pipeline uses 1m buckets). This leads to boundary conditions during bursts.

harry: Proposed tactical fixes:
- Implement a reconciliation job that compares enforcer counters vs canonical counters and flags orgs where enforced_429s >> canonical_429s.
- Add an alert: ratio(enforcer_429s / canonical_429s) > 3 for 5m.

yuki: I'll add a Graf panel: enforcement_rejects vs metered_rejects + consumer_lag. Also create an alert rule when consumer_lag > 3m AND reject_ratio > 2. Owner: yuki, ETA: EOD.

andrea: Longer-term: change enforcer to switch into a "grace" mode when ingestion lag is high — allow small extra burst (e.g., +20% tokens) and throttle to steady state rather than hard-reject. That reduces customer-facing 429s while still bounding spend. We need telemetry to measure risk.

sam: Risk: grace-mode leaks budget. Alternative: emit "shadow-accept" header for requests allowed under grace, but keep returning normal responses to customer. That preserves visibility but might not help customer 429s. Another idea: when lag high, prefer soft-deny (return 429 but mark X-Reason: "ingest-lag") so downstream agents can retry differently.

mira: For data integrity we should also build a replay/backfill runner that can rehydrate ledger state for affected orgs (replay last 1h of topic into ledger and recompute aggregates). I'll prototype consumer that replays and writes CDC to ledger table. Owner: mira, ETA: 48h.

harry: Proposed reconciler quick algorithm:
1) periodically compute diff = enforcer_local_counts - canonical_counts for (org, window)
2) if diff > threshold (e.g., 5% or 1000 tokens) mark org for backfill and emit an incident event
3) apply corrective action: refresh enforcer cache OR run one-off replay to ledger
We can run in shadow first. Owner: sam, ETA: 3 days.

andrea: Operational changes:
- Add a dashboard panel showing the top 10 orgs by discrepant rejects, consumer lag, and recent burst rates.
- Add a 5m alert: consumer_lag > 5m AND reject_ratio > 2.
- Dogfood staging with injected 10m lag and run through quota flows.
Owners: yuki (dashboard/alerts), sam (reconciler), mira (replay).

yuki: Will post Graf links here when ready. Also I can add a lightweight alert that triggers a runbook recommending toggling enforcer grace mode.

sam: Quick debug commands for enforcer nodes:
```
# inspect reserved budget for org
curl -s "https://enforcer.internal/admin/inspect?org=acme-corp" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" | jq '.reserved_budget'
# check recent rejects
curl -s "https://enforcer.internal/admin/logs?org=acme-corp&minutes=15" | grep quota_reject | tail -n 20
```

mira: I'll also test lowering clickhouse flush window from 30s -> 10s for a staging shard to see impact on end-to-end latency.

andrea: Action items recap: 1) yuki: add panels + alerts (EOD) 2) sam: prototype reconciliation and diff-based backfill (3d) 3) mira: replay runner + flush tuning (48h) 4) andrea: canary config for grace-mode + dogfood (1w). Dev owners assigned.

devops-bot: Created ticket P12345 and linked this thread: https://jira.redwood.internal/browse/P12345

andrea: :thumbsup: Thanks all — keeping thread open for status updates. Will post staging dogfood results here.

yuki: :eyes: will update once grafana panels + alerts are live.

harry: :shipit: starting prototype for reconciler tomorrow morning.
